title: Tensoring over a constant field sheaf commutes with cohomology
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], small relative to the universe of its module sheaves, let $\kappa$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $\kappa_{\mathcal C}$ be the constant sheaf of rings with value $\kappa$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $C^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of sheaves of $\kappa_{\mathcal C}$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] and $N$ a sheaf of $\kappa_{\mathcal C}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $C^\bullet\otimes_{\kappa_{\mathcal C}}N$ for the complex with terms $C^q\otimes_{\kappa_{\mathcal C}}N$ and differentials $d^q\otimes1$, the tensor product being that of sheaves of modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and for a complex $D^\bullet$ of $\kappa_{\mathcal C}$-modules write $\mathcal H^i(D^\bullet)=\operatorname{Ker}(d^i)/\operatorname{Im}(d^{i-1})$, computed in the abelian category of sheaves of $\kappa_{\mathcal C}$-modules. Then for every integer $i$ there is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\kappa_{\mathcal C}$-modules
$$\mathcal H^i(C^\bullet)\otimes_{\kappa_{\mathcal C}}N\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal H^i(C^\bullet\otimes_{\kappa_{\mathcal C}}N),$$
natural in $C^\bullet$ and $N$, which on local sections sends $[z]\otimes y$ to $[z\otimes y]$.

proof.text: Let $P$ be the constant presheaf of rings with value $\kappa$, so $P^\#=\kappa_{\mathcal C}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Restrict the action on $N$ along $P\to P^\#$ and call the resulting presheaf of $P$-modules $F$. Its underlying abelian presheaf is already a sheaf. The sheafification interface [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] therefore gives $F^\#\cong N$ as $P^\#$-modules: the underlying sheafification of an already sheaf object is itself, and the compatible extended action is unique. On each object $U$, $F(U)=N(U)$ is a vector space over $\kappa$; no claim that $\kappa_{\mathcal C}(U)=\kappa$ is needed.

For every $U$, [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective] makes $F(U)$ projective over the field $\kappa$, and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] makes it flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring with $F(U)$ preserves the exact sequence $0\to\ker f\to V\xrightarrow{f}W$, so it preserves kernels. It preserves finite products: for two factors the inverse to the comparison sends $(v\otimes y,w\otimes z)$ to $(v,0)\otimes y+(0,w)\otimes z$, extended additively; the tensor relations show that both composites are identities. The empty product is zero and $0\otimes F(U)=0$. Equalizers are kernels of differences, so these comparisons give every finite limit. Limits of presheaves of $P$-modules are computed objectwise: compatible tuples and their scalar action and restriction maps give the limiting presheaf directly. Consequently the presheaf functor $-\otimes_{p,P}F$ preserves finite limits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat] to the presheaf ring $P$ and presheaf module $F$ of Step 1, using the finite-limit preservation proved in Step 2. It says that $F^\#$ is a flat $P^\#$-module. With $P^\#=\kappa_{\mathcal C}$ and $F^\#\cong N$, this is exactly flatness of $N$. By the definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], flatness here means that $T_N:G\mapsto G\otimes_{\kappa_{\mathcal C}}N$ is an exact functor on the category of sheaves of $\kappa_{\mathcal C}$-modules. This category is abelian under the smallness hypothesis [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Fix $i\in\mathbf Z$ and apply clause (c) of [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] to $C^{i-1}\xrightarrow{d^{i-1}}C^i\xrightarrow{d^i}C^{i+1}$ and the exact functor $T_N$ of Step 3. Its canonical comparison identifies the kernel of $d^i\otimes1$ with $T_N(\ker d^i)$ and the image of $d^{i-1}\otimes1$ with $T_N(\operatorname{im}d^{i-1})$, compatibly with the cycle inclusions and quotient projections. Invert the resulting isomorphism $\mathcal H^i(T_NC^\bullet)\cong T_N(\mathcal H^i(C^\bullet))$ to obtain the displayed isomorphism. The cited clause also gives naturality for chain maps $C^\bullet\to D^\bullet$. There is no boundedness restriction: this application uses only the indicated three consecutive terms.

proof.text: For a cycle section $z$ and a section $y$ of $N$ over the same object, the cycle inclusion after tensoring sends $z\otimes y$ to the same pure tensor in $C^i\otimes N$. Compatibility with the quotient projection in Step 4 therefore gives $[z]\otimes y\mapsto[z\otimes y]$. If $z$ changes by a boundary $d^{i-1}w$, its image changes by $(d^{i-1}\otimes1)(w\otimes y)$, also a boundary. For a morphism $u:N\to N'$, both composites of the naturality square send this generator to $[z\otimes u(y)]$. These equalities hold on sums of pure tensors and then on their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Cycle classes locally generate cohomology because the quotient by the image is a sheafified cokernel [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus the equalities determine the morphisms of sheaves and prove naturality in $N$, completing joint naturality with Step 4.
